To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the epithelial sodium channel γ-subunit protein is expressed in fibrous astrocyte processes in the CVO borders, the white matter (including the optic nerve and optic chiasm), and the ventral medullar surface, and that these cells may be important in sodium homeostasis.
a novel group of ENaC-γ-expressing fibrous astrocyte cells have been found in the CVO borders and along the ventral medullar surface.
a group of glial cells, which express the γ-subunit of the epithelial sodium channel, is concentrated in the white matter, the pia mater, and along the borders of several circumventricular organs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of novel glial cell subtypes, the functions of which are not yet known.
the discovery of the ENaCγ-expressing astroglial cells in the CVO, white matter, ventral medulla, and pia mater.
the identification of a group of fibrous ENaC γ-positive astrocytes that are distributed in the circumventricles, the white matter, and in the ventral medullae of rodents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ENaC γ-positive glial cells are located at strategic sites in the brain that are involved in sodium homeostasis, and that these cells have the capacity to regulate extracellular Na+ concentration.
these ENaC γ-positive astrocytes are involved in the control of sodium homeostatic mechanisms and may play a role in sodium regulation in the brain.
the ENaC-expressing astroglia are a unique group of glial cells with the ability to regulate sodium homeostasis in the CNS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ENaC γ is expressed in a novel population of astrocytes in regions where sodium homeostasis is regulated.
the glial cells in the circumventicular organs, white matter and ventral medulla surface express ENaC γ and serve as sites for sodium buffering and sodium regulation.

the astrocytes that express ENaC γ-protein in circumventricular organs may be involved in sodium regulation by glial and neural cells, and that the white matter astrocytes may serve as a buffer of Na+ for saltatory conduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ENaC-expressing astroglia are not confined to the epithelium, but are found throughout the brain, including the CVOs and white matter.
the ENaC subunit proteins are expressed in astrocytes, not only in the brain but also in other tissues.
the ENaCγ-expressing astroglia may play a role in sodium regulation.
